```sql
WITH lines AS (
  SELECT pv.product_id,
         o.id       AS order_id,
         pv.id      AS variant_id,
         ol.quantity,
         ol.line_total_cents
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = o.id
    JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
   WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
     AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
     AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
     AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
totals AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         sum(quantity)         AS quantity,
         sum(line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents
    FROM lines
   GROUP BY product_id
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT product_id, count(*) AS order_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, order_id FROM lines) d
   GROUP BY product_id
),
variant_counts AS (
  SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM lines) d
   GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       oc.order_count,
       t.quantity,
       t.revenue_cents,
       vc.variant_count
  FROM totals t
  JOIN order_counts   oc ON oc.product_id = t.product_id
  JOIN variant_counts vc ON vc.product_id = t.product_id
  JOIN products p        ON p.id = t.product_id
 ORDER BY t.quantity DESC, t.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De `count(DISTINCT ...)` op ruim 81k regels, die nu een externe sort op (p.id, o.id) veroorzaakte, is vervangen door `DISTINCT`-vooraggregaties die met een hash-aggregatie kunnen. De join met `products` gebeurt pas op het aggregaat (ca. 1.751 groepen), en de aggregaattypes blijven gelijk, dus het resultaat is identiek. Gelijke waarden in de ORDER BY blijven, net als in het origineel, niet-deterministisch geordend.
